bloques.html: Hay muchos tipos de castillos de arena: grandes, pequeños, hechos por manos de niños, por manos de arquitectos, algunos se los lleva en seguida la marea, otros duran semanas, y al final todos sucumben a la entropía. bloques.html:
En el Concilio de Nicea (325 d.C.) se elaboró el Credo, que describe la filiación divina de Jesucristo diciendo que Él y el Padre son de la misma sustancia. San Juan también empieza su evangelio hablando de cómo Cristo es el principio creador del universo.

Cristo es la arena de la que está hecho el Universo. Pero a diferencia de la arena, no es una sustancia inerte, sino que es la consciencia misma, la luz que ilumina el mundo y que te permite conocerlo en este instante. Es el elemento subjetivo, es ese “yo” constante en el centro de tu experiencia al que la sabiduría nos llama a conocer.

Por otro lado, aquí estamos tú y yo: seres humanos de carne y hueso, con una pantalla delante, sentados aquí, en un mundo aparentemente hecho de materia. Somos castillos de arena que nacen, cambian y se disuelven. En este nivel nos ponemos nombres: Antonio, Juan, Betül, Jesús… nombres que parecen encapsular ese “yo” en un cuerpo. Todo lo externo al cuerpo no soy “yo.”

Pero cuando uno cierra los ojos e investiga en profundidad ese “yo,” no tarda en descubrir que, en realidad, no se refiere al castillo, sino a la arena. Esencialmente somos arena: la consciencia que es a la vez inmutable y sustancia del mundo cambiante

La única diferencia entre Jesús y nosotros es que Jesús, cuando decía yo, se refería exclusivamente a la arena. No aceptó nada temporal, nada sujeto a la entropía, como limitación de su identidad. Él se quedó solo con lo eterno, aceptó plenamente su naturaleza divina como Hijo consustancial al Padre. Eso no implica que rechazase su naturaleza humana, todo lo contrario, esta alcanzó su máxima expresión en ese yo sin límites.

La cuestión es, ¿quiénes somos tú y yo? ¿Somos los castillos, o somos la arena?

Si digo yo soy el castillo, he elegido identificarme con el cuerpo. Eso es el ego, fiel creyente en el dios de la separación, que me dice que al final de esta vida limitada me espera la muerte. El que pone su mente al servicio del ego, solo ve castillos y las guerras y romances que ocurren entre sus habitantes. El que mira de ese modo, nunca se percata de la omnipresencia de la arena.

Ahora, si digo yo soy la arena, he elegido creer en el Dios de Jesús, y entonces la muerte es solo un cambio más, no un final. Sigo viendo los castillos, pero ya no están definidos por sus formas variables, sino por la arena única. El que mira de este modo, solo ve a Cristo. La marea vendrá y se llevará este castillo, pero la arena permanece.

Al decir yo soy la arena, ya no estoy mirando al cuerpo humano con el que tiendo a identificarme, estoy mirando a la sustancia de la que está hecha mi experiencia completa en este instante. Hay otras personas en mi experiencia ahora. Escribo desde un avión. Oigo a un bebé llorar, la luz de la mañana entra por las ventanillas: nubes, cielo azul, el mar Mediterráneo: todo hecho de la arena de la consciencia, todo es “yo,” todo es Cristo radiante.

El cuerpo de Antonio aparece, cambia durante años y algún día desaparecerá. Lo mismo ocurrirá con la voz que suena en mi mente y que dice ser yo. Pero esa voz no es yo, son solo frases escritas en la arena, un extraño poema sobre miedos, anhelos, y arándanos. Castillos. Formas que surgen y desaparecen. ¿Qué permanece? La arena, la consciencia, el yo atemporal que compartimos con Jesús y con el Padre.

Jesús nos dijo: Niégate a ti mismo.

También nos invitó a rezar diciendo: Santificado sea Tu nombre (refiriéndose al Padre).

Ambas ideas convergen: yo soy la arena eterna, no el castillo temporal.

Limpia tu nombre, tu sentido del “yo,” de lo que aparece en tu experiencia, eso viene y va, pero yo siempre soy yo. Quédate solo con lo que permanece. Vuelve al reconocimiento de que la vida eterna ya está aquí, y eres tú, disfrazado de tiempo.

El cuerpo seguirá siendo tuyo, pero ahora estará guiado por una mente integrada, no una dividida. Tu día a día estará guiado por el Espíritu Santo, no por Legión.

Tus pasos por este mundo dejarán escrito un poema de amor en la arena, una llamada a los demás castillos a reconocer “tú eres yo.” Y cuando la marea se lleve el castillo, nada esencial habrá cambiado, nada esencial se habrá perdido, la arena permanecerá. El Hijo, al fin sin disfraz, volverá a abrir sus ojos al rostro feliz del Padre.

en.extracto: There are many kinds of sandcastles: large, small, built by children's hands, by architects' hands, some swept away quickly by the tide, others lasting weeks, and in the end all of them…

bloques.html: There are many kinds of sandcastles: large, small, built by children's hands, by architects' hands, some swept away quickly by the tide, others lasting weeks, and in the end all of them surrendering to entropy. Forms that appear, endure for a time, and dissolve. But the sand, the substance, that remains.
bloques.plano: There are many kinds of sandcastles: large, small, built by children's hands, by architects' hands, some swept away quickly by the tide, others lasting weeks, and in the end all of them surrendering to entropy. Forms that appear, endure for a time, and dissolve. But the sand, the substance, that remains.

bloques.html:
At the Council of Nicaea (325 AD), the Creed was drawn up, describing the divine filiation of Jesus Christ by saying that He and the Father are of the same substance. Saint John also opens his gospel speaking of how Christ is the creative principle of the Universe.

Christ is the sand of which the Universe is made. But unlike sand, he is not an inert substance. He is consciousness itself, the light that illuminates the world and allows you to know it in this instant. He is the subjective element, that constant "I" at the center of your experience that wisdom calls us to investigate.

And then, here we are, you and I: human beings of flesh and blood, with a screen in front of us, sitting here in a world that appears to be made of matter. We are sandcastles that are born, change, and dissolve. At this level we give ourselves names: Antonio, Juan, Betül, Jesus... names that seem to encapsulate that "I" inside a body. Everything outside the body is not "me."

But when one closes one's eyes and investigates that "I" in depth, it does not take long to discover that, in reality, it does not refer to the castle but to the sand. Essentially we are sand: the consciousness that is at once unchanging and the substance of the changing world.

The only difference between Jesus and us is that when Jesus said "I," he was referring exclusively to the sand. He accepted nothing temporal, nothing subject to entropy, as a limitation of his identity. He stayed only with the eternal, fully accepting his divine nature as the Son consubstantial with the Father. That does not mean he rejected his human nature. On the contrary, it reached its fullest expression in that boundless I.

The question is: who are you and I? Are we the castles, or are we the sand?

If I say I am the castle, I have chosen to identify with the body. That is the ego, faithful believer in the god of separation, which tells me that at the end of this limited life death awaits. The one who puts his mind in service of the ego sees only castles, and the wars and romances that play out among their inhabitants. The one who looks that way never notices the omnipresence of the sand.

But if I say I am the sand, I have chosen to believe in the God of Jesus, and then death is just one more change, not an ending. I still see the castles, but they are no longer defined by their variable forms, only by the one sand. The one who looks this way sees only Christ. The tide will come and carry the castle away, but the sand remains.

In saying I am the sand, I am no longer looking at the human body with which I tend to identify. I am looking at the substance of which my entire experience in this moment is made. There are other people in my experience now. I am writing from an airplane. I hear a baby crying, the morning light comes through the windows: clouds, blue sky, the Mediterranean Sea, all made of the sand of consciousness, all "I," all radiant Christ.

The body of Antonio appears, changes over years, and one day will disappear. The same will happen with the voice that sounds in my mind and claims to be me. But that voice is not me. It is only a name written in the sand, a strange poem about time fears, longings, and blueberries. Castles. Forms that arise and dissolve. But what remains? The sand, consciousness, the timeless I that we share with Jesus and with the Father.

Jesus told us: Deny yourself.

He also invited us to pray saying: Hallowed be Thy name (referring to the Father).

Both ideas converge: I am the eternal sand, not the temporary castle.

Cleanse your name, your sense of "I," from what appears in your experience. That comes and goes. But I am always I. Stay only with what remains. Return to the recognition that eternal life is already here, and it is you, dressed up as time.

The body will still be yours, but now it will be guided by an integrated mind, not a divided one. Your daily life will be guided by the Holy Spirit, not by Legion.

Your steps through this world will write a love poem in the sand, a call to the other castles to recognize: you are me. And when the tide carries the castle away, nothing essential will have changed, nothing essential will have been lost. The sand will remain. The Son, at last without disguise, will open his eyes again to the happy face of the Father.
